answer: Daily attention checkpoints require every identity to answer short unpredictable prompts at random times for a week, and a missed prompt resets its standing. An attacker must therefore keep a distinct operator or capable agent watching each identity through the full week, paying real attention time per clone instead of a one-time fee. The schedule uses a relic near the meadow and a ridge marker as unrelated landmarks, so no shared shortcut carries attention across identities.
